exemplar.run: recorded run of Testuary 0.2.0 on JSONCompare.java, 2026-11-12

vocabulary.collection_rule: JUnit 4 runs the methods annotated with ``@Test`` (``org.junit.Test``) of the test class.
vocabulary.import_rule: declares the target's package and uses the target class directly
vocabulary.load_error_patterns:
- cannot find symbol -> import the class from its package, or fix
    the name of the class, method or field.
  - package ... does not exist -> import only packages the project or
    its test dependencies provide.
  - incompatible types / cannot be applied to given types -> pass the
    types the target's signatures declare.
  - unreported exception ... must be caught or declared to be thrown
    -> declare the test method ``throws Exception``.
  - ';' expected / reached end of file while parsing -> check the
    working file for unbalanced braces or parentheses and stray
    characters from a previous edit.
vocabulary.parse_error_hints: missing semicolon or closing brace, unbalanced parentheses or quotes, a statement outside a method, accidental code-fence remnants
vocabulary.single_file_rule: Produce one test class in one ``.java`` file, named for the class, in the target's package. Do not create helper files.
vocabulary.stands_alone_advice:
1. A test file must compile and run on its own: declare in it
     every helper class it uses, not in another test file.
  2. A test class must set up what it needs in its own ``@Before``
     or ``@BeforeClass`` methods, not rely on what another test class
     leaves behind (static fields, singletons, files it writes).
  3. A test must restore what it changes beyond itself in
     ``@After``: static fields and singletons, System properties,
     the default Locale and TimeZone.
vocabulary.test_dependencies:
Test toolkit (always available):
  - JUnit 4 (``org.junit.Test``, ``org.junit.Assert``)
The project's own classes and its declared test dependencies are also available; other libraries are available only if the project's build declares them.
vocabulary.validity_rule: Allowed: the target's runtime behaviour and its API, including reflection on its classes (getDeclaredMethods, getAnnotations). Forbidden: reading its source file (the .java file through Files, a reader or stream, a Scanner or getResource) or its compiled class file (the .class bytes through getResource or a file), or declaring a type named like its class, which would test a copy in its place.
